'''Ryszard Winiarski''' (March 2, 1936 – December 4, 2006) was a Polish painter and [[Scenic design|set designer]] best known for his [[Monochrome|monochromatic]] [[Abstract art|abstract]] geometric compositions and spatial forms.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Gorządek |first=Ewa |date=March 2006 |title=Ryszard Winiarski |url=https://culture.pl/en/artist/ryszard-winiarski |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=Culture.pl |publisher=Adam Mickiewicz Institute |place=Warsaw |language=en |issn=1734-0624}}</ref> He has been associated with [[Conceptual art|Conceptualist]] tendencies in Poland during 1960s and 1970s and is considered one of the key representatives of [[indeterminism]] in Polish postwar art. Winiarski's work was informed by his interest in the relationship between art and science.<ref name=":0" />

== Life and work ==
[[File:Ryszard Winiarski, Sto zdarzeń 10x10.jpg|thumb|''One hundred events 10x10,'' 1977]]
Ryszard Winiarski was born in [[Lwów]], then part of the [[Second Polish Republic]], on March 2, 1936.<ref name=":0" /> He studied at the [[Warsaw University of Technology]] from 1953 to 1959, graduating with a master's degree in precision mechanics. Subsequently, he pursued studies in painting under [[Aleksander Kobzdej]] at the [[Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw|Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts]] from 1958 to 1966. He later worked at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts as a lecturer and, between 1985 and 1990, as the vice-dean.<ref name=":0" /> In his art, Winiarski combined [[Constructivism (art)|constructivist]] principles focused on geometry with elements of [[probability theory]]. This approach included the use of certain mathematical systems to compose and create visual forms.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Rozmarynowski |first=Łukasz |date=2020-12-20 |title=Abstrakcji przestrzeń wieloraka. Kategoria przestrzenności w twórczości Wojciecha Fangora, Jerzego Grabowskiego i Ryszarda Winiarskiego - studium porównawcze |url=https://pressto.amu.edu.pl/index.php/aq/article/view/26396 |journal=Artium Quaestiones |volume=31 |issue=1 |pages=401–436 |doi=10.14746/aq.2020.31.13 |issn=0239-202X|doi-access=free }}</ref>{{Rp|page=426}}

Winiarski experimented with chance and probability by composing [[Abstract art|abstract]] arrangements of small squares, initially in black-and-white and later in color.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gryglewicz |first=Tomasz |date=2012 |title=Abstrakcja geometryczna w krakowskim środowisku artystycznym w latach 1960-2010. |url=http://cejsh.icm.edu.pl/cejsh/element/bwmeta1.element.desklight-a285cda0-55c9-4950-91c7-9a44423b24ee |journal=Quart. Kwartalnik Instytutu Historii Sztuki Uniwersytetu Wrocławskiego |volume=3 |language=PL |issue=25 |pages=54–67 |issn=1896-4133}}</ref> Winiarski regarded the anonymous building blocks of a small square as "statistical material" from which to build the surface of the work.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rotzler |first=Willy |title=Constructive Concepts: A History of Constructive Art from Cubism to the Present |publisher=Rizzoli |year=1989 |isbn=978-0-8478-1024-6 |location=New York |pages=207 |language=en}}</ref> In 1966, Winiarski wrote: "My ambition involves attempts at visually recording events and presenting their [[Probability distribution|statistical distributions]] visually. The multitude of possibilities that such treatment of the image offers fascinates me".<ref name=":1" />{{Rp|pages=404–405}} Between 1967 and 1977, Winiarski created set designs for several plays performed in Poland, including ''Medea'' by [[Euripides]], [[William Shakespeare]]'s ''[[Othello]]'' and ''[[Macbeth]]'', among others.<ref name=":0" />

In 1987, he initiated the creation of geometric compositions using lit candles, a series titled ''Geometry, or a Chance for Meditation''. Winiarski's works are included in permanent collections of major Polish museums, including the [[Museum of Art, Łódź|Museum of Art in Łódź]] and the [[National Museum in Kraków]].<ref name=":0" /> Similarly to his contemporary [[Roman Opałka]], Winiarski dedicated the majority of his career to exploring a singular [[Conceptual art|conceptual]] project.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Szabłowski |first=Stach |date=2017-06-05 |title=Artysta systemu |url=https://przekroj.org/sztuka-opowiesci/artysta-systemu/ |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=[[Przekroj]] |language=pl}}</ref> In 1995 he received [[Jan Cybis Award]].<ref name="cybisrecipients">{{citeweb| url = https://owzpap.pl/laureaci-nagrody-im-jana-cybisa/| title = Laureaci Nagrody imienia Jana Cybisa| publisher = owzpap.pl| accessdate = 2026-04-25| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20260425120822/https://owzpap.pl/laureaci-nagrody-im-jana-cybisa/| archive-date = 2026-04-25}}</ref> According to art historian and critic Bożena Kowalska, Ryszard Winiarski was among the most influential Polish artists in the second half of the twentieth century.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kowalska |first=Bożena |date=2016-09-19 |title=O Ryszardzie Winiarskim – nie tylko wspomnieniowo |url=https://www.tygodnikpowszechny.pl/o-ryszardzie-winiarskim-nie-tylko-wspomnieniowo-35697 |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=[[Tygodnik Powszechny]] |language=pl}}</ref> Winiarski died in Warsaw on December 14, 2006, at the age of 70 following a long illness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Małkowska |first=Monika |date=2006-12-14 |others=Originally published in ''[[Rzeczpospolita]]'' |title=Warszawa. Odszedł Ryszard Winiarski |url=https://encyklopediateatru.pl/artykuly/32883/warszawa-odszedl-ryszard-winiarski |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=Encyklopedia Teatru Polskiego |language=pl}}</ref>
